Absence returns OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than a negative prohibition answer or positive selected-control compliance answer. An intentionally restricted assessment domain and misplaced substantive conditions remain competing interpretations. Unknown scope also blocks otherwise decisive result facts.

Both offer-level candidates separate offer-wide promotional linkage from existence of a non-discount gift. The promotional connection must attach to the same gift component; otherwise an unrelated gift in a mixed offer could be caught. Negative aggregation also requires sufficient component coverage and preservation of unresolved classifications, which node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 does not expressly specify.

The circular defines distributors through SFC-authorised fund distribution while quoting a Code restriction referring to investment products generally. Implementing the circular's context and implementing the broader Code provision are distinct alternatives; broader application requires the external text and an explicit scope decision.

Gift and discount classifications remain supplied judgments. Additional returns or incentives are not automatically gifts; absence of a structured-product finding is not a gift exemption. A discount in another component cannot exempt a distinct gift.

For node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249, provider must identify the offering distributor rather than merely a funder or fulfiller. The circular regulates offering without requiring receipt or payment, but does not comprehensively resolve third-party attribution.

FALSE, OUT_OF_SCOPE and compliance with the selected gift control do not establish general legal permission. Advertising and other controls remain separate. The supplied material also does not establish a concrete effective-date interval or applicable versions of external standards.
